relevance_review.label: Child Stunting (% under 5)
relevance_review.description: Height-for-age < -2 standard deviations from the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Key marker of chronic undernutrition and structural deprivation in early childhood.
relevance_review.source: UNICEF / WHO / World Bank Joint Malnutrition Estimates (March 2026)

relevance_review.label: Child Overweight (% under 5)
relevance_review.description: Weight-for-height > +2 standard deviations from the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Emerging form of paediatric malnutrition signaling nutrition transition.
relevance_review.source: UNICEF / WHO / World Bank Joint Malnutrition Estimates (March 2026)

relevance_review.label: Child Wasting (% under 5)
relevance_review.description: Weight-for-height < -2 standard deviations from the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Acute malnutrition indicator reflecting rapid weight loss or failure to gain weight.
relevance_review.source: Global Nutrition Report (Country Nutrition Profiles Feb 2023)

relevance_review.label: Adult Obesity (%)
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Primary driver of metabolic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and cardiovascular morbidity.
relevance_review.source: Global Nutrition Report (Country Nutrition Profiles Feb 2023)

relevance_review.label: Adult Diabetes (%)
relevance_review.description: Fasting blood glucose >= 7.0 mmol/L or on medication for raised blood glucose.
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Major metabolic chronic outcome directly linked to dietary quality and adiposity.
relevance_review.source: Global Nutrition Report (Country Nutrition Profiles Feb 2023)

relevance_review.label: Anaemia in Women of Reproductive Age (%)
relevance_review.description: Haemoglobin concentration < 120 g/L for non-pregnant and < 110 g/L for pregnant women.
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Pivotal indicator of micronutrient deficiency (iron, folate) affecting maternal-child health.
relevance_review.source: Global Nutrition Report (Country Nutrition Profiles Feb 2023)

relevance_review.label: Low Birth Weight (% of live births)
relevance_review.description: Birth weight strictly less than 2,500 grams (up to and including 2,499 g).
relevance_review.public_health_relevance: Early life proxy for intrauterine growth restriction and maternal undernutrition.

preprocessing_log.child_anaemia_exclusion_reason: Prevalence of anaemia in children under 5 correlates strongly (r = 0.8982) with anaemia in women of reproductive age. Retaining both would overweight haemoglobin deficiency relative to chronic and acute anthropometric measures. Child anaemia is retained as a validation and context metric.

selection.rule_specification: Among K=3..6, select highest silhouette score; tie-break lower Davies-Bouldin; require mean bootstrap ARI >= 0.60.
selection.rationale: Selected K=3 (K-Means, Euclidean): Achieved the highest silhouette score (0.3266) among K in [3..6] with a Davies-Bouldin index of 1.2443, satisfying the stability requirement with a mean bootstrap ARI of 0.9278 >= 0.60.

complete_case_analysis.finding: K-Means clustering on 121 complete cases achieves an ARI of 0.9340 against the 156-country KNN-imputed baseline, demonstrating high structural consistency.

limitations: Data years vary across indicators and countries, reflecting asynchronous national survey schedules (e.g. DHS/MICS) and global reporting cycles.
Child malnutrition estimates for 2024 from JME represent modelled point estimates and carry uncertainty intervals.
Adult obesity and diabetes indicators aggregate modelled female and male estimates from the Global Nutrition Report.
Wasting represents acute malnutrition at survey time and can exhibit seasonal and crisis-driven volatility.
Clustering identifies mathematical similarity in multivariate space and must not be interpreted as policy compliance or clinical diagnosis.
responsible_use: Health organizations should utilize peer benchmarks as starting points for bilateral peer learning, not competitive rankings.
Indicator deltas should guide targeted contextual inquiry rather than prescriptive policy mandates.
Double-burden designations flag concurrent high levels relative to this dataset, warranting integrated policy approaches to undernutrition and overnutrition.
